title: Forces and Spaces Between Particles
summary: Why gases can be squashed into cylinders, why sugar 'disappears' into water, and how strongly particles hold on to each other.

cbse.chapter: Curiosity Ch 7: Particulate Nature of Matter (interparticle attraction and spaces)
Earlier NCERT: Matter in Our Surroundings (not in Exploration 2026)

objectives: I can describe the interparticle forces of attraction and spaces in solids, liquids and gases.
I can explain compressibility using the particle model.
I can use evidence (dissolving, compressing, breaking) to support the idea of spaces and forces between particles.
misconceptions: When a gas is compressed, the particles themselves get smaller.
Liquids can be squashed easily like gases.
Sugar is destroyed when it dissolves.
